title: Dear Colleague Letter: Prohibition on Collaborations with Restricted Entities (NSF 26-022)
date_evidence: Dateline under the H1: "July 8, 2026"; footer: "Publication date: July 8, 2026" and "Last updated: July 8, 2026"; publication number NSF 26-022
key_claim: On 8 July 2026 NSF gave notice of a policy, to be implemented in Fiscal Year 2027, under which NSF funds may not be used for research in collaboration with entities on twelve U.S. restricted-party lists (including the BIS Entity List, the Section 1260H and 1286 lists, OFAC lists, the FCC Covered List, the UFLPA Entity List and CBP Withhold Release Orders) or with their employees; senior/key personnel may not hold positions with or take support from such entities during an award; NSF says risk mitigation for such projects is not sufficient and that the rule aligns with the Department of War's approach.
frame_summary: NSF frames the change as a move from risk mitigation to outright prohibition for listed entities, justified by the government's own listing decisions and by consistency with the Department of War, and presented as reducing administrative burden rather than adding to it.
verbatim_quote: NSF appropriated funds shall not be used for grants, contracts, other transactions or other assistance to an organization if the purpose is to conduct research in collaboration with restricted entities. This funding prohibition also extends to the employees of such restricted entities.
verbatim_list: Therefore, NSF has determined research security risk mitigation for NSF-funded projects involving these restricted entities is not sufficient.

By aligning this prohibition with the Department of War's approach to collaborations with entities on U.S. restricted party lists, NSF seeks to safeguard NSF-funded research while promoting consistency and reducing administrative burden.
NSF intends to implement this prohibition in Fiscal Year 2027

To comply with this prohibition once it is effective, organization Authorized Organizational Representatives (AORs) and senior/key personnel will be required to certify to this effect at the time of proposal submission.
notes: Primary policy notice. The count of twelve lists is the analyst's tally of Appendix A (1260H; 1286; Entity List; Military End-User; Denied Persons; EO 14032 Annex; NS-CMIC; Debarred Parties; Nonproliferation Sanctions; FCC Covered List; UFLPA Entity List; CBP Withhold Release Orders and Findings). title: The Department of War Releases Updated List of Foreign Institutions Engaging in Problematic Activities to Counter Unauthorized Technology Transfer
date_evidence: Release dateline under the H1: "July 23, 2026 |"; body: "The Department of War today announced the publication of the Fiscal Year (FY) 2025 update to the list of foreign institutions"
key_claim: On 23 July 2026 the Department of War published the FY2025 update of the Section 1286 list, which identifies 130 academic and research institutions in China, Russia and Iran, and advised strict caution for domestic researchers, institutions and industry partners considering collaboration, funding or data-sharing with any listed institution; the list will be updated at least once a year.
frame_summary: The Department presents the list as a counter-technology-transfer instrument aimed at institutions confirmed to raise the risk of misappropriation of U.S.-funded research, and extends its cautionary reach beyond defence contractors to all domestic researchers and industry partners.
verbatim_quote: The FY25 list formally identifies 130 academic and research institutions located in China, Russia and Iran.
verbatim_list: The Department advises strict caution for domestic researchers, academic institutions and industry partners when considering collaboration, funding or data-sharing engagements with any institution named on this list.
The Department will continue to update the list at least once a year or as appropriate based on emerging intelligence and threat assessments.

title: Department of War Orders Research Security Audits at 30 Academic Institutions
date_evidence: Release dateline under the H1: "Aug. 17, 2026 |"; body: "Institutions are required to report their findings and actions directly to the Department no later than August 31, 2026."
key_claim: On 17 August 2026 the Department of War notified 30 U.S. academic institutions to review their academic, financial and research collaborations with entities on the Section 1286 list and with organisations linked to rebranded Confucius Institutes; to stay eligible for future federal research funding they must audit every identified collaboration, assess exposure of sensitive or export-controlled research and implement mitigation plans including termination of partnerships, reporting to the Department by 31 August 2026.
frame_summary: The Department frames university partnerships with listed foreign institutions as a research-security exposure to be audited and, where necessary, terminated, with future federal funding eligibility as the lever and Congress as a partner in the effort.
verbatim_quote: To maintain eligibility for future federal research funding, the notified universities must complete a comprehensive audit of all identified foreign collaborations, assess the exposure of sensitive or export-controlled research, and implement strict mitigation plans, including the termination of problematic partnerships. Institutions are required to report their findings and actions directly to the Department no later than August 31, 2026.
verbatim_list: The Department of War has issued formal notifications to 30 domestic academic institutions, directing them to initiate immediate and comprehensive reviews of their academic, financial and research collaborations with foreign entities of concern.
"The Department of War has zero tolerance for academic partnerships that compromise our national security," said Emil Michael, Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering.

publisher: White House Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP)
title: National Security Science & Technology Strategy (NSSTS), August 2026
date_evidence: PDF title page: "National Security Science & Technology Strategy August 2026"; file path /uploads/2026/08/NSSTS-082026.pdf; Nextgov (17 August 2026) reports the document was "publicly released on Monday", i.e. 17 August 2026
key_claim: The August 2026 NSSTS lists, among measures to strengthen research security, prohibiting fundamental research funding to high-risk entities including companies on the Section 1260H list, automated research security vetting of proposals and continuous monitoring of funded projects, and states that through technology prosperity deals the United States and key partners have committed to share practices for identifying and mitigating threats to the research enterprise and to lead allies and partners toward similarly rigorous practices.
frame_summary: OSTP frames research security as one pillar of a strategy to protect national-security science from theft and exploitation while keeping the enterprise open and productive, and treats list-based funding prohibitions, automated vetting and allied alignment as the next steps beyond NSPM-33.
verbatim_quote: Prohibiting fundamental research funding to high-risk entities, including companies on the section 1260H list of Chinese military companies operating in the United States;
verbatim_list: Developing automated research security vetting of proposals for agency-funded research and continuous monitoring of funded research projects, where appropriate;

Through the technology prosperity deals, the United States and key partners have committed to share practices and information for identifying and mitigating threats to the research enterprise. Cooperation will include building capacity at research entities, strengthening threat analysis in key technology areas, and leading allies and partners toward similarly rigorous practices.
America’s R&D enterprise remains open and is more secure as a result of NSPM-33.
We will adopt approaches that protect without inhibiting the productivity and agility of the national security S&T enterprise.
notes: PDF; the provenance audit cannot read PDFs and the sandbox has no egress. Text read from the WebFetch PDF extraction on 16/09/2026 (line breaks in the PDF removed). Release day taken from Nextgov's dated coverage; the document itself carries only "August 2026".

publisher: China International Science and Technology Exchange Center (CISTE, 中国国际科技交流中心)
title: 10月1日起，美国国家科学基金会（NSF）禁止资助项目与部分中国高校合作
key_claim: CISTE, the international-exchange arm of the China Association for Science and Technology, reads the NSF notice as taking effect from 1 October 2026, notes that NSF published no new China list but reused existing U.S. restricted-party lists, names the seven defence-linked universities and other institutions on the BIS Entity List, records that the Section 1260H list covers 188 Chinese entities as of June 2026, and stresses that not all China-US research cooperation stops, since the rule bites only on NSF-funded projects; it describes the shift as one from risk management to access restriction.
frame_summary: CISTE frames the NSF rule as a decisive change in U.S. research-security policy from risk management to access restriction, presents it to Chinese readers as list-driven rather than country-driven, and counsels that cooperation outside NSF funding may continue.

从更长远来看，这项政策也意味着，美国科研安全政策正从过去强调"风险管理"，逐步转向更加严格的"准入限制"模式。

title: White House S&T strategy calls for new approaches to safeguard US research (Edward Graham)
key_claim: The NSSTS was publicly released on Monday 17 August 2026; it calls on research institutions to conduct automated research security vetting of agency-funded proposals and continuous monitoring of funded projects, and on the same day the Pentagon announced that 30 academic institutions must review their ties with foreign entities; the strategy also calls for attracting global talent, a departure from the 2025 National Security Strategy.
frame_summary: Nextgov frames the strategy as a call for novel security measures across the research enterprise while noting a tension with the administration's earlier hostility to foreign talent.
verbatim_quote: But the strategy says research institutions need to take further steps to enhance their threat awareness, including conducting “automated research security vetting” of agency-funded research proposals and performing continuous monitoring of federally-supported projects.
verbatim_list: The Trump administration says the nation’s science and technology research ecosystem needs to embrace “novel security solutions” to ensure the U.S. maintains its global edge, according to a new document publicly released on Monday.

title: Buitenlandse wetenschappers toch niet massaal gescreend op spionagerisico
date_evidence: <meta property="og:article:published_time" content="2026-06-11T20:20:34+0200">; visible dateline "NOS Nieuws•donderdag 11 juni, 20:20"
key_claim: On 11 June 2026 the Dutch education minister, Rianne Letschert, told parliament the government would not after all screen some 8,000 foreign researchers and students a year under the knowledge-security screening bill, because advice showed it did not meet the criteria of effectiveness, feasibility and proportionality, would jam the system, and could not lawfully be confined to non-EU researchers; instead about €80 million extra is made available to 2031 for institutions' own precautions, the Knowledge Security Desk is expanded, and TU Delft's advisory team already handles about 700 cases a year.
frame_summary: NOS frames the reversal as a retreat from state-run screening to institution-run risk assessment on grounds of workability, cost and non-discrimination, with the threat itself undisputed and the minister promising a narrower design after the summer.
verbatim_quote: De overheid gaat toch geen 8000 buitenlandse wetenschappers en studenten per jaar screenen om spionage te voorkomen.
verbatim_list: Maar uit ingewonnen adviezen blijkt dat de screening niet aan "de criteria van effectiviteit, uitvoerbaarheid en proportionaliteit voldoet", schrijft de minister nu.
Zo stelt ze tot en met 2031 zo'n 80 miljoen euro extra beschikbaar zodat kennisinstellingen voorzorgsmaatregelen kunnen treffen, zowel digitaal als fysiek.
Op de TU Delft bijvoorbeeld krijgt het adviesteam inmiddels ongeveer 700 zaken per jaar voorgelegd.
Letschert belooft na de zomer met een update te komen.
notes: Dutch-language Tier 3 (public broadcaster) reporting the minister's letter to parliament (Kamerstuk 2026D29090, same day). publisher: 科技日报 (Science and Technology Daily)
title: 正听丨NSF涉华实体禁令严重损害中美科技合作 (胡定坤)
date_evidence: Visible dateline under the H1: "2026-07-14 01:45:00 来源: 科技日报"; URL path carries /2026-07/13/
key_claim: The commentary in the Ministry of Science and Technology's newspaper argues that neither the BIS Entity List nor the 1260H list bans research cooperation with Chinese entities (published fundamental research is exempt from export controls, 1260H only bars entry to the U.S. military supply chain and the FCC list only covers products), so NSF is stretching the lists' scope; it notes NSF supplies about a quarter of government basic-research funding to U.S. universities, warns of a chilling effect on non-NSF and unlisted cooperation, and cites a Quincy Institute estimate of a 20% fall in China-US co-authored papers between 2017 and 2024.
frame_summary: The paper frames the NSF rule as an illegitimate extension of trade and procurement lists into academic cooperation that will harm the United States as much as China, and presents Chinese science as rising regardless of decoupling.
verbatim_quote: 事实上，无论是BIS实体清单还是1260H清单，都没有禁止与中国实体的科研合作。NSF此举是在肆意扩展清单的限制范围，将国家安全概念泛化到科研合作领域。
verbatim_list: NSF是美国最主要的科研资助机构之一，资助额约占美国高校基础研究领域政府拨款的四分之一。
更严重的是，作为掌握科研经费分配大权的政府部门，NSF此举极易在美学术界引发"寒蝉效应"，导致美国科研机构和研究人员对华合作意愿整体降低，非NSF资助或与未被纳入清单的中国实体的合作项目也会受到波及。
禁令公布第二天，美国众议院"中国问题特别委员会"主席约翰·穆勒纳尔毫不掩饰地评论道，禁止将联邦资金用于与构成国家安全风险的中国实体合作是明确清晰的，美国各政府机构应以此为"榜样"。
notes: State-media commentary (MOST's newspaper), Tier 4, used directionally for the Chinese official-side objection that the lists were never collaboration bans; not used as an anchor for any figure.
